stimulus.description: Mean oxygen released in 2 minutes (milliliters) ± 2SE for a catalase-catalyzed reaction at three levels of temperature. n = 10 replicates per level.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe how the oxygen released in 2 minutes changes across the three levels of temperature, and identify the level with the greatest oxygen released in 2 minutes. Use values from the table to support your description.
parts.model_answer: The oxygen released in 2 minutes peaks across the levels (5.2, 16.4, 2.6); it is greatest at 37 °C (16.4).

rubric_rows.criterion: One description of the pattern across the levels, supported by table values (the level with the greatest value is part of the description)
required_elements: A description of how the mean changes across the three levels, supported by table values and naming the level with the greatest mean
alt_solutions: rises then falls
highest at the middle level
common_errors: describes only one pair of levels
describes a trend the data do not show
names a level that is not the greatest
rubric_rows.grading_note: Table interpretation (skill 4.B): no biology concept is required for this point.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the percent change in the oxygen released in 2 minutes from 70 °C to 37 °C. Show your work.

rubric_rows.criterion: Percent change with work shown (answer)
required_elements: Computes the percent change correctly with a valid method (new minus old, divided by old, times 100)
alt_solutions: percent change = (new - old) / old x 100
common_errors: divides by the new value
forgets to multiply by 100
rubric_rows.grading_note: Quantitative analysis (skill 5.A): award for the correct value with a valid method; equivalent forms and rounding within the tolerance are accepted. No biology concept is required.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Using the ±2SE values, determine whether the difference between the mean oxygen released in 2 minutes at 37 °C and at 10 °C is statistically supported. Justify your answer with the ±2SE ranges.
parts.model_answer: 37 °C: 14.16 to 18.64; 10 °C: 4.42 to 5.98. The ranges do not overlap, so the difference is supported.

rubric_rows.criterion: States whether the difference is supported and justifies it by comparing the ±2SE ranges of the two levels
required_elements: Correctly states whether the difference between the two levels is statistically supported
Justifies by comparing the ±2SE ranges of the two levels (overlap or separation)
alt_solutions: the ranges are separated so the difference is supported
compares the mean ± 2SE intervals of the two levels
common_errors: compares only the means
states the wrong conclusion for the ranges
rubric_rows.grading_note: Statistical reasoning (skill 5.B): no biology concept is required for this point.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain why the oxygen released in 2 minutes is lower at 70 °C than at 37 °C. Use data from the table as evidence and connect it to what you know about enzymes.
parts.model_answer: At 70 °C the mean is 2.6 compared with 16.4 at 37 °C. temperature far from the enzyme's optimum reduces activity (too cold: fewer effective collisions; too hot: denaturation changes the active site), which explains the lower value in the data.

rubric_rows.criterion: One reasoned explanation that connects the data (the lower value at the stated level compared with the highest) to the effect of the condition on enzyme shape and active site, so activity is reduced
required_elements: A single reasoned explanation that connects the data (the lower value at the stated level compared with the highest) to the effect of the condition on enzyme shape and active site, so activity is reduced
alt_solutions: the condition at the lower level changes the enzyme's shape, so substrate binds less well, which is why the table shows the lower value
denaturation of the enzyme at that level reduces the rate seen in the data
common_errors: cites the numbers but gives no biological reason (evidence without reasoning)
gives the mechanism with no reference to the data (reasoning without evidence)
attributes the lower value to the substrate running out or to the enzyme being used up
rubric_rows.grading_note: ONE explanation completed by a claim-evidence relationship (skill 6.C: reasoning that connects evidence to theory). Award the point only when the response connects the data to the enzyme-structure mechanism in one explanation. Data alone or mechanism alone earns no point: these are the two halves of one explanation, not separately scored elements.

weakness_attribution.note: Parts A-C are data skills only; do not aggregate them as enzyme-concept mastery. Only part D contributes to concept-level (topic 3.2) evidence.
